patch.value: Recoveries rendered for an SDK runAction or MCP call with its own cwd keep the caller's relative --pm-path, so replaying them from the host's directory can target a different tracker

Found 2026-11-11 by the Codex review of PR 1705, against the pm-pwqiao note-recovery retry; the same shape applies to every recovery built with resolvePmCommandScopeArgs. resolvePmCommandScopeArgs deliberately preserves an explicit tracker path's spelling, which is the portable scope convention from pm-gh1611. A CLI invocation and its retry share one working directory, so that is safe there. An SDK runAction({ cwd: '/tmp/w', path: '.' }) or an MCP call that names its own cwd runs under that directory, but the retry it returns says --pm-path . and is replayed from the host's directory. That selects another tracker, possibly one holding the same id. Relative link paths and globs in the replayed command anchor the same way. Duplicate check: searched recovery, cwd, runAction and --pm-path; pm-gh1611, pm-szn67i and pm-p316vn (closed) fixed portability, nested aliases and flag preservation, not a differing execution directory.

A recovery rendered while runAction or an MCP call ran under a cwd different from the host's names the tracker so that replaying it from the host selects the same tracker; Relative link paths and globs in such a replay resolve as the original call resolved them; CLI recoveries keep their portable relative spelling
A recovery returned by an SDK or MCP call replays against the tracker that call used
The retry keeps --pm-path . from the call's cwd, which selects the host's tracker when replayed
